metadata.title: Key to Common Problems of Tomatoes
metadata.geographic_scope: General tomato symptom screening and growing practices.
metadata.review_notes: General symptom patterns and prevention practices. Excludes geographically specific prevalence or treatment.

passages.section: Symptoms on Leaves and Stems, Leaf Yellowing and Leaf Spots
passages.content: Yellow margins can surround some leaf spots. Yellowing between veins can indicate a nutrient problem. Yellow lower leaves with wilting can be associated with wilt disease.

passages.section: Symptoms on fruits - blotches or discolored areas, Blossom end rot
passages.content: A dark, leathery depression at the blossom end can indicate blossom-end rot. Calcium can be insufficient in growing fruit tissue under stress such as irregular or shallow irrigation. Maintain steady watering and mulch, and check soil pH before amending.

metadata.title: Tomato leaf spot diseases
metadata.review_notes: Approved general sanitation and moisture-management practices only. No chemical treatment recommendation.

passages.content: Water the soil at the base of plants, cover soil with mulch to reduce splashing, support plants for airflow, and handle plants after the foliage dries.
